Truthfully one of the most disappointing experiences I've had with an NBA game. The first few hours were okay, learning the new shot meter and getting used to playing 2K again after not touching 24. I first had major problems even getting my controller to work with the game and spent 30 minutes trouble shooting just to find out my sim wheel and pedals were causing the issue. Another major issue I had was if my controller disconnected for any reason and reconnected the game would either crash or stall for at minimum two minutes before resuming.

Over the next few days I had minor issues with crashes but they were infrequent, I mostly noticed that if I navigated any of the menus too quickly or tabbed out of the game it would crash. I tried playing today (third day of ownership and 5th game into MyCareer) and the game would consistently crash after ~15 minutes. I tried multiple workarounds, fixes, etc. and couldn't find a result that fixed the issue.

Even after this game has been out for this long the game is still unpolished for PC and riddled with random problems. This edition is further cementing my choice to avoid 2K in general with their consistent failures to make a proper port for a PC title.

This game draws heavily on the CPU, it doesn't use your GPU. This caused me to have a message in the top left of my screen that says low vram. You can turn this message off in the settings but the players names were blurry. It seemed like the game ran worse the more I edited rosters or downloaded created players from the internet. I asked for a refund.

Short version: Thank god 2K FINALLY upgraded this game to next-gen, a little slow to start, but runs and plays perfectly fine.

Long version: So, 2K FINALLY realized that pumping out old-gen games to PC is hurting their sales and reviews, and finally gave us next-gen for PC. About time.

The game does take a little while to run consistently well because of shaders and stuff, but once it gets going with all of it's visual assets and other things, it runs and plays rather well, consistently getting around 70-80 FPS.

It's also one of the few games on Steam where I can actually use my controller without relying on Steam Input, which is a nice bonus, and makes my experience much better.

I know some people may say I was paid by 2K to make a positive review, but I was not. This is my honest-to-god opinion about a game FINALLY getting with the times and putting respect on PC's name.
